key_insight: A large language model can substantially improve its own code-generation performance by fine-tuning on its raw sampled outputs (no external teacher, verifier, or reinforcement learning required). Simple self-distillation (SSD) raises pass@1 significantly (e.g., Qwen3-30B-Instruct from 42.4% to 55.3%).
problem_solved: How to improve LLM code generation without needing additional labeled data, a stronger teacher model, program verifiers, or RL-based pipelines—reducing engineering and compute complexity for model improvement.
method: Generate multiple solution samples from the model using specific temperature and truncation settings to increase diversity.
Aggregate the raw sampled outputs (no external verification or teacher labels) and create a supervised fine-tuning dataset from them.
Fine-tune the same model on this self-generated dataset (simple self-distillation) to yield improved correctness, particularly on harder problems.
impact: SSD offers a low-complexity, low-overhead recipe to boost code-generation accuracy using only the model itself, enabling practitioners to get large performance gains without extra annotation, verifiers, or RL infrastructure.
visual_elements: Before/after bar chart: pass@1 (%) for the base model vs SSD-fine-tuned model (e.g., 42.4% → 55.3%).
Process diagram: loop showing 'model samples code' → 'assemble samples' → 'supervised fine-tune same model' → 'improved model'.
Difficulty breakdown: stacked bars or heatmap showing larger gains on harder problems.
Icon set: 'no teacher', 'no verifier', 'no RL' with cross-out symbols to emphasize simplicity.
paper_title: Embarrassingly Simple Self-Distillation Improves Code Generation
paper_authors: Ruixiang Zhang, Richard He Bai, Huangjie Zheng, Navdeep Jaitly, Ronan Collobert
